name: Prepare the monthly progress draw
summary: Each month the project team of a general contractor bills the owner for the work done on one project. The assistant project manager collects trade billings, the superintendent and project manager walk the site to agree percentages against the schedule of values, the project accountant reconciles and issues a proper invoice with a statutory declaration and WSIB clearance, and the prime consultant certifies the amount. It is slow because it waits on trades, on site walks and on the consultant, and error-prone because percentages are judgment calls that consultants cut.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor with about 220 active building projects, an Ontario head office and regional project teams, billing owners monthly under CCDC 2 or owner-written contracts.
baseline.notes: Ontario's prompt payment rules applied to contracts entered after 1 October 2019; earlier contracts and the western and Atlantic regions billed under contract terms with consultant certification first. The steps are the same; the legal weight of the delivery date differs.

unit_of_work: one monthly progress draw for one project
trigger: The month's progress update from site coordination and the approaching billing cut-off (about the 20th to 25th).
end_state: The consultant has certified the draw, the certified receivable and holdback are booked, and collections has the draw.

volume.seasonality: One draw per active project per month all year; slightly fewer active projects in January and February when fewer projects start.

evidence.note: One draw per active project; 220 active projects from the organisation file's active-projects driver.

resources.name: Site office trailers and sea containers

steps.name: Collect subtrade pencil billings
steps.description: The assistant project manager emails the 15 to 30 active subcontractors a reminder of the billing cut-off, then collects each trade's draft progress billing by the 25th from email and the project platform, chasing the late ones by phone so their percentages can roll into the owner draw.

error.defect_description: A trade's billing is missing or claims more than it has installed.

evidence.note: Practice in Canadian GCs of passing subtrade progress billings into the owner draw; 15-30 trades per active building project and a 25th-of-month cut-off are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Travel to site for the draw walk
steps.description: The project manager, who usually runs two projects from the regional office, drives to site for the monthly walk with the superintendent, timing the visit to the billing cut-off and the superintendent's availability around pours and inspections.

evidence.note: Regional office PMs visiting sites at least monthly; drive times of 30-120 minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Walk the site to assess percent complete
steps.description: The superintendent walks each floor and area with the project manager and the schedule of values printout, estimating the percentage installed for each line (concrete, steel, envelope, mechanical rough-in) and challenging trade percentages that look ahead of what is physically in place.

error.defect_description: Percent complete overstated on lines that are hard to see (concealed services, stored materials).

control.basis: Site orientation and PPE for all persons entering an active site (Ontario O. Reg. 213/91)

evidence.note: Monthly site assessment of percent complete against a schedule of values is common GC practice; superintendent's role in it is the author's estimate. The organisation file does not list the superintendent on this process.

steps.name: Update the schedule of values with percentages
steps.description: The assistant project manager types the agreed percentages into the schedule of values billing workbook or the ERP progress billing screen line by line, and checks that no line exceeds 100% and that stored materials are supported by invoices.

error.defect_description: Keying error or a line billed past 100%.

evidence.note: Excel schedule of values or ERP progress billing module common in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Add approved change orders to the draw
steps.description: The assistant project manager opens the change order log, adds each change order the owner signed since the last draw as a new billing line, and bills the percentage complete of change work, leaving pending quotations and disputed changes out.

error.defect_description: A pending (unsigned) change is billed, which the consultant will strike.

evidence.note: Applications for payment include approved change work; billing pending changes is a common cause of reductions.

steps.name: Reconcile the draft draw to job cost and trade billings
steps.description: The project accountant compares the draft draw with costs posted in job cost and the trade billings in AP by cost code, looking for underbilling (cost ahead of billing) and overbilling, checks the 10% holdback calculation and HST, and returns questions to the project team.

control.basis: Finance review of billings before issue; 10% holdback retained under the Construction Act and contract

evidence.note: Holdback and proper invoice content; reconciliation to job cost is the author's description of common practice.

steps.name: Review the draft draw and adjust
steps.description: The project manager reviews the reconciled draft, weighs how far to push percentages on front-loaded lines against the risk of the consultant cutting them, decides on underbilled lines, and either signs off or sends it back for changes.

error.defect_description: Aggressive percentages left in that will be cut later.

evidence.note: Share of drafts sent back is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Send the pencil draw to the consultant
steps.description: The project manager emails the pencil (draft) draw with the schedule of values and change order list to the prime consultant and the owner's project representative, asking for comments before the formal application is issued.

evidence.note: Pencil draw review before formal submission is widespread Canadian practice; not stated in an opened source.

steps.name: Wait for consultant comments on the pencil draw
steps.description: The prime consultant's contract administrator compares the pencil draw with what they saw at the last site meeting and their own site review notes and replies with agreed values or line-by-line comments.

evidence.note: Consultant turnaround and share of drafts with comments are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Meet the consultant to settle disputed lines
steps.description: The project manager meets the consultant in the site trailer or walks the areas in question, explains the percentages and stored materials, agrees revised values line by line, and notes what will be carried to next month's draw.

evidence.note: Meeting length and frequency are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Prepare the formal application and invoice
steps.description: The project accountant creates the progress billing invoice in the ERP receivables module, prints the application for payment on the owner's or CCDC form with the agreed values, computes holdback and HST, and assembles the backup the contract requires.

error.defect_description: Application form does not match the contract's proper invoice requirements.

evidence.note: Monthly application to consultant and owner; proper invoice content under Construction Act s. 6.1.

steps.name: Download a current WSIB clearance certificate
steps.description: The project accountant logs into the WSIB clearance portal, downloads the company's current clearance certificate, checks that its validity period covers the invoice date, and attaches it to the application as workers' compensation evidence.

control.basis: CCDC 2-2020 GC 5.2: workers' compensation evidence with each application; WSIB clearance policy 14-02-19

evidence.note: Clearance valid up to 90 days; evidence required with each application after the first.

steps.name: Draft the statutory declaration
steps.description: The project accountant fills in the CCDC 9A statutory declaration, checking in AP that every subcontractor and supplier included in the previous draw has been paid, and lists any amounts withheld under a notice of non-payment.

error.defect_description: Declaration states trades are paid when one payment is still outstanding.

control.basis: CCDC 2-2020 GC 5.2: CCDC 9A statutory declaration with each application after the first

evidence.note: CCDC 9A with each application under CCDC 2-2020 (under CCDC 2-2008 only at holdback release).

steps.name: Sign the statutory declaration and approve release
steps.description: The operations manager, as an officer with signing authority, reviews the draw total and the declaration, swears the declaration before a commissioner of oaths in the office, and approves the application for release.

control.basis: Officer signature on sworn declarations and billing approval under the delegation of authority

evidence.note: Signing by an officer (here the operations manager) is the author's estimate of common delegation; the organisation file does not list the operations manager on this process.

steps.name: Issue the proper invoice to consultant and owner
steps.description: The project accountant emails or uploads the signed application, invoice, statutory declaration and clearance to the consultant and the owner on the same day, recording the delivery date because it starts the 28-day payment clock.

control.basis: Ontario Construction Act s. 6.1-6.4: proper invoice delivered monthly; owner pays within 28 days

next.condition: P3 or lender-funded project needing a certifier package

evidence.note: 28-day payment clock from proper invoice; simultaneous delivery under CCDC 2-2020. P3 share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the P3 certifier and lender package
steps.description: On P3 and lender-funded projects the project manager assembles the monthly progress report for the independent certifier or lender's technical advisor, with photos, schedule status and cost-to-complete, so Project Co can draw construction financing.

evidence.note: P3 payment mechanics via independent certifier are the author's general knowledge; no opened source.

steps.name: Wait for the consultant's payment certificate
steps.description: The consultant reviews the formal application against its own site observations and the contract, then issues a certificate for payment, sometimes reducing lines, or returns the application if documents are missing.

next.condition: returned as not a proper invoice

evidence.note: Consultant turnaround and outcome shares are the author's estimates; CCDC 2-2008 gave the consultant 10 days to certify (not confirmed in an opened source).

steps.name: Review consultant reductions
steps.description: The project manager compares the certified amount with the application, decides whether to accept each reduction and re-bill it next month or dispute it, and tells the project accountant how to record the difference.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Correct and reissue the application
steps.description: The project accountant fixes what the consultant rejected, such as an expired clearance, a missing declaration page or a wrong holdback figure, and reissues the corrected package, which restarts the payment clock.

evidence.note: A non-proper invoice does not start the 28-day clock.

steps.name: Record the certified amount in the ERP
steps.description: The project accountant adjusts the receivable invoice to the certified amount, issuing a credit note for any reduction, and books the holdback receivable so the billing, holdback and job cost records agree.

error.defect_description: Holdback receivable booked at the wrong amount.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Hand the certified draw to collections
steps.description: The project accountant emails the certificate and invoice reference to the billing and collections specialist, who tracks the payment due date, and notes any disputed reduction that may need a notice or adjudication.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: File the certificate and roll the schedule of values forward
steps.description: The assistant project manager files the certified draw package in the project document store and rolls the schedule of values forward so next month's draw starts from the certified percentages rather than the applied ones.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Pencil draw disputed by the consultant
exceptions.description: The consultant comments on some lines and the project manager meets them to agree values before the formal issue.

exceptions.name: Consultant reduces the certified amount
exceptions.description: Lines are cut at certification; the PM decides to re-bill next month or dispute, and the accountant books a credit note.

exceptions.name: Application returned as not a proper invoice
exceptions.description: A missing declaration, expired clearance or wrong form means the package is reissued and the payment clock restarts.

exceptions.name: P3 certifier package
exceptions.description: On P3 projects a progress report for the independent certifier or lender's adviser is added before certification.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the billing cut-off reminder to the certified draw being filed
benchmarks.population: Monthly progress draws on Canadian building projects, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: trade billings by the 25th, formal issue around the 1st to 5th and certification within about 10 days of issue, a common contract pattern.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from proper invoice to owner payment
benchmarks.population: Ontario construction contracts entered after 1 October 2019 and CCDC 2-2020

evidence.note: Statutory and standard-form deadline; tier B because taken from law firm summaries, not the Act.

pain_points.description: Late trade billings hold up the whole draw; the owner draw cannot be built until the main trades submit.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Percent complete is negotiated twice, once at the pencil review and again at certification, and reductions push cash into the next month.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

pain_points.description: Paper statutory declarations need an officer's signature before a commissioner, which waits on the officer's calendar.

evidence.note: Declaration required with every application under CCDC 2-2020.

assumptions: Loaded costs come from the organisation file (1.35 loading on salaried wages).

The superintendent and the operations manager are included because the percent-complete walk and the sworn declaration need them; the organisation file lists only the project manager, assistant project manager and project accountant on this process.
Owner payment and notices of non-payment are documented in fin-owner-receivables; this workflow ends at certification.

The simulated median cycle time (21.6 days, p90 26.4) is close to the 20-day estimate; the simulated p90 is a little tight because real consultant turnaround has a longer tail than a triangular range shows.
Staffing: the stated FTEs (29.6) match touch time x volume; about 17 hours of staff time per draw is the author's estimate.
Self-perform labour is not billed separately; it sits inside schedule of values lines.

sources.title: Prompt Payment for Construction in Ontario
sources.supports: Construction Act Part I.1 in force 1 October 2019 for contracts entered after that date; proper invoice monthly unless the contract says otherwise and cannot depend on certifier action; owner pays within 28 days; owner notice of non-payment within 14 days; contractor pays subcontractors within 7 days of receiving payment, or 35 days after the proper invoice unless it gives notice; undertaking to adjudicate within 21 days.

sources.title: The new CCDC 2 - 2020: contract changes you need to know
sources.supports: Monthly applications for payment to the consultant and owner simultaneously; workers' compensation evidence and a CCDC 9A statutory declaration with each application after the first; owner pays within 28 days (20 days under CCDC 2-2008); holdback paid no later than 10 working days after the holdback period expires; consultant responds to a Ready-for-Takeover application within 10 days.

sources.title: Clearance Certificate in Construction (Operational Policy Manual document 14-02-19)
sources.supports: A principal that retains a construction contractor must have a clearance in place for the whole time the contractor works; a clearance is valid for up to 90 calendar days and is renewable; without one the principal may be liable for the contractor's WSIB obligations up to the labour portion of the contract; records kept 3 years; policy applies from 1 January 2020.
